scope.hash_policy: Decisive checks cite the catalog view_sha256 of the source handle plus line ranges. Excerpt hashes were not computed (the evaluator toolset has no shell); the host validates JSON and hashes.

facets.text: 0.5 = Zarr v3 zarr.json with metadata under attributes.ome and version "0.5", distinct from legacy 0.4 Zarr v2 .zattrs flat attributes
version MUST be consistent within a hierarchy; inconsistent declared versions must be detected
admission requires explicit compatibility validation or a truthful unsupported result for legacy, missing or inconsistent versions
no implicit legacy reinterpretation (reference readers silently switch to the detected format with only a log warning, or fall back to flat attrs)
distinguishing check: equivalent-looking v3/0.5 vs legacy container, plus inconsistent-version hierarchy
axes length equals array rank; axis order constraints (time, channel/custom, space)
unique axis names; array dimension_names MUST match axes names
navigation/slicing tied to validated axis identity, not fixed 5D positions, shape or conventional names; axis names arbitrary
distinguish absent dimensions from length-one dimensions
facets.decisive: S003 81, 296-302 (2-5D, optional time/channel); S034 70 (real challenge image shape 1,1,1,93184,144384); S033 333-337 (converter TCZYX default)

facets.text: reject rank/dimension_names mismatches without inventing sliders or coordinates
datasets list is authoritative: ordered highest resolution first; paths group-relative; names arbitrary
level-specific geometry from each level's own transform; no fixed factor-of-two; non-power-of-two and anisotropic (e.g. Z not downsampled) reductions
no lexicographic or numeric folder ordering
explicit handling of a declared level whose array is missing or unreadable
selection UI/performance policy remains a product choice
composition order: each dataset's list applied in order (scale then optional translation), then multiscales-level transforms
calibrated coordinates include offsets (translation), not array indices or scale alone
units come from axes (SHOULD, UDUNITS); a missing unit means unknown calibration; units must not be invented
scale may be a relative factor to the first level when physical scaling is unavailable, so it cannot always be shown as physical size
concrete check that exposes reversed composition or omitted offsets (hand-computed expected coordinates)
discovery through the labels group 'labels' key (MUST key; all label images SHOULD be listed); intermediate groups allowed; names arbitrary
label image is multiscales with the same number of levels as the source
declared association: image-label.source.image relative path (default ../../) resolved to the source image before overlaying
level/coordinate relationship via transforms; label dimensions equal the image's or 1; never attach by folder basename or equal array dims alone
unsupported or mismatched geometry stays explicit
labels are integer categorical values from 8 integer dtypes including uint64/int64
colors/properties keyed by label-value, not array position
preserve categorical identity through decode/lookup/resampling (no interpolation creating new IDs; exact integers including uint64 beyond binary64 range)
facets.decisive: S003 434-439; S025 84-86 (Viv lacks 64-bit integers); S048 706-708 (separate labels layer type)

facets.text: or declare an exact supported range and refuse unsupported label data
specified colors are a reader SHOULD, not a universal format mandate

unsupported_claims.location: s1 B-015 (P11 corrected: 'hard-codes dimorder T,C,Z,Y,X (S098 line 256), a correctness risk'); B-045 reason ('AGAVE's risky fixed dimorder')

unsupported_claims.location: s1 B-014 (P10 CONFIRMED: napari 'resolves arbitrary entry points by walking up, and tolerates rotation/affine/sequence transforms with warn-and-skip'); B-030 (F1 corrected constraint: 'arbitrary entry-point walk-up (S048 lines 672-689)')

novel_supported_findings.claim: The resave default shard shape is the full image array; shards over 100,000,000 pixels need an explicit --output-shards, so single whole-array shards are expected in challenge-lineage filesets.
novel_supported_findings.plan_fit: F9 decode matrix / F7 memory bounding (Plan L7, L9)

novel_supported_findings.claim: Real interop failures on 0.5-era data: neuroglancer 'no multiscale metadata' plus a single-shard array with no chunks and no error; vizarr #307 repetitive chunks on resave-converted 0.5; napari/ome-zarr zarr<3 pin conflict. The viewer must explain these and never go silent.

novel_supported_findings.claim: HCS-at-scale precedents: vizarr shows the lowest-resolution plate and opens a clicked well in a new window; napari crashes on zoom; MoBIE supports plates (no detail); ome-zarr-py zero-fills stitched grids. So plate navigation is a product choice with overview-plus-drill-down favoured.
novel_supported_findings.plan_fit: Plan L5 image listing / L7 responsiveness

novel_supported_findings.claim: bioformats2raw.layout discovery precedence (plate, else OME series, else numbered groups); readers SHOULD surface all images.
novel_supported_findings.plan_fit: Plan L5 'lists the images it finds'

novel_supported_findings.claim: HCS plate/row/well/field hierarchy with sparse plates, so a flat list is wrong and navigation must be hierarchy-aware.
omero render defaults are optional (color/active/label/window, greyscale whitening); a single bad window must degrade per channel, unlike ome-zarr-py's wipe-all.

novel_supported_findings.location: s1 B-021 (P16 corrected), B-091 (O-C3); s4 N1
novel_supported_findings.claim: Multiple multiscales per group: the spec allows user choice with first as fallback; 10/11 surveyed viewers report supported:no, 3 fail to open, OMERO is ambiguous.

AGAVE's OME-Zarr Load Settings dialog (resolution level, channel exclusion, X/Y/Z sub-region, GPU memory estimate) is an explicit bounding alternative to fully automatic loading, so pyramid UX is a product choice.
novel_supported_findings.plan_fit: Plan L5 level choice / L7 responsiveness

novel_supported_findings.claim: AGAVE's <=4 channels / 16-bit / first-time-sample / few-GB limits come from TIFF/CZI-era docs and must not be cited as OME-Zarr behaviour (modulo X1-U3 on time).
Reference-reader timeline: PR404 0.5 read-only (Nov 2024), v0.12.0 writing (Aug 2025), v0.15.0 deprecations + 0.5 download fix, v0.16.0 sharding, v0.19.0 permissive-0.5/scene/plain-string codecs.
The ome-ngff-validator plus IDR/challenge sample catalogs give a pre-check oracle for a representative fixture matrix (validator coverage itself unknown, R7).
AGAVE's scene count equals the multiscales list size, one scene per multiscales entry.
Both reference readers hide labels by default.
Session settings must avoid the absolute-path portability trap documented for AGAVE.
novel_supported_findings.plan_fit: Plan L9 display settings local to session

novel_supported_findings.claim: The mixed v04/v05 exception is write-path only. On read, ome-zarr-py detects the format, logs 'version mismatch: detected/requested' and silently switches to the detected format, so Slide Scout's version errors must be its own and must not copy the silent switch.

unsupported_claims.location: s1 B-009 (P6 corrected: 'conforming groups MUST carry the string value "3"'; verifier reason: 'the layout value is the string "3" in S003, not the bare number 3')
unsupported_claims.type: overstated source fact (lost ambiguity); the verifier reason is partly contradicted
unsupported_claims.counterevidence: S003 200 and 213: the 0.5 spec's own JSON examples use the integer 3; so does the 0.4 spec (S059 255, 261). Only the prose at S003 256 quotes "3". The spec is ambiguous and doesn't clearly require a string type.
unsupported_claims.consequence: A type-strict check built from this sentence would reject spec-example-shaped (integer-valued) bioformats2raw collections and hide their images.

unsupported_claims.location: s1 B-050 (F5 corrected constraint: 'for plates, derive label metadata from the first well/first field and label data from the plate-wide lazy pyramid helper')
unsupported_claims.counterevidence: S048 507-555 is a napari implementation shortcut, not a spec rule. X2 itself notes the per-well behaviour isn't verifiable (plate.py absent, S047 200). S003 740-752 allows heterogeneous wells/fields.
unsupported_claims.consequence: Heterogeneous plates would get first-well label metadata. X1 routes the same fact to an explicit product decision instead.

unsupported_claims.location: s1 B-060 (CONFIRMED: 'corpus proves both automatic background/cancel (Plan) and explicit pre-load bounding')
unsupported_claims.counterevidence: No corpus source implements background loading with cancellation. S103 (AGAVE #84) describes loading that 'blocks the whole application and is not easy to cancel' as an open request.
unsupported_claims.consequence: Suggests a precedent exists for a Plan behaviour that has none, which weakens the case for extra validation of the cancel path. The Plan still specifies the behaviour.

unsupported_claims.location: s4 N6 ('The 0.5 spec says label images are "usually" same-dimensions (S003 lines 432-433) without this rule')
unsupported_claims.counterevidence: S003 106-108: 'Each dimension of the label should be either the same as the corresponding dimension of the image, or 1 if that dimension of the label is irrelevant.' S058 333-337 copies the 0.5 spec layout ('See OME-Zarr 0.5 spec').
unsupported_claims.consequence: Frames a spec-stated relationship as a converter/consumer nuance. The rule itself is correct.

comparison_X1_vs_X2.summary: Same reference outcome (C01 retained, C02-C08 narrowed) with no status difference, so no critical loss separates the two. X2 fixed two inherited reader-code misdescriptions and added more verified code-level findings, but its verifier also introduced more new errors (7 X2-only, including the moderate-low string-typed layout claim and a plate-label constraint) and a heavier, partly redundant question list. X1 kept more validation ideas in section 1 and corrected the background/cancel overstatement, but it kept two draft misdescriptions of napari and made one false dismissal. No fractional or net score is given.
